items.context: @FefeDemeny (Fefe Demeny, 70.247 seguidores), en inglés: "Why the realized price of Bitcoin does not matter". Argumenta que el realized price (~$54k) es menos confiable este ciclo: el volumen spot en BTC cayó ~72% desde 2022, más del 60% de los coins comprados vía ETF nunca se movieron (costo base ETF ~80K), así que el realized price se actualiza lento; puede seguir siendo piso amplio, pero la regla de "tocarlo primero" es menos segura. Publicado hace ~14 min: 26 likes, 2 reposts, 7 respuestas, 2.431 vistas. Tema temperatura de mercado / valoración.
items.suggested_text:
Fair point, and it's the best argument for never leaning on a single on-chain anchor. MVRV is just market price over realized price, so if realized price reprices slowly because ETF coins barely move, the ratio inherits the same blind spot.

That's why I prefer blending independent lenses: MVRV, price against the 200-week average, drawdown from the high, and volatility-adjusted 90-day momentum, 25% each. Even with all four mixed, my Market Temperature reading went from 99.29 to 0.67 in 364 days, about as cold as that scale gets.

What a cold reading can't tell you is how long the cold lasts, and that's usually where "it must tag level X first" rules quietly break. https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2122727211610542288
